subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB346. RULE (three halves): (i) a record identified for access locked by ANOTHER file connector => the operation's result depends on the presence or absence of the RETRY phrase; (ii) RETRY present => 'additional attempts may be made to read the record as specified in the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase'; (iii) 'The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase.' VALIDATED: `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.9.30.4 "If the RETRY phrase is not specified or the record is not successfully accessed as specified by the RETRY phrase, the record operation conflict condition exists"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.7.9.3 "the result of the evaluation of arithmetic-expression-1 or arithmetic-expression-2 is negative or zero, the statement is unsuccessful"` -> OK 14.7.9.3 4) a); `--check 9.1.13.8 "an attempt to access a record that is currently locked by another file connector"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 1); `--check 9.1.13.8 "The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 2). IMPLEMENTATION: FileRegistry.ConflictOnLockedRecord is the ONE GR9 conflict check, reached from ReadShared (Format 1) and from ReadKeyedShared (Format 2), each BEFORE its physical retrieval (every connector names the record its next read would make available, FileConnector.PeekSequentialRecordId and PeekRandomReadRecordId), for all three organizations; it contributes only the conflict predicate and the status assignment and delegates BOTH of GR9's second and third sentences to RetryLoop, whose landing goes through ExhaustionStatus. The four RETRY forms are four different rules with three distinct grounds and one shared landing: no phrase and a negative-or-zero arithmetic-expression-1/-2 are 14.7.9.3 GR4 a); n TIMES is GR4 b) -> GR1 with an exhausted count; FOR n SECONDS is GR4 b) -> GR2, whose timeout period is clamped to this implementation's maximum meaningful value of ZERO (Annex A.1 item 166, docs/CONFORMANCE.md 7), so it makes no attempt either; all four land the closing paragraph's 'appropriate value ... according to the rules for 9.1.13', i.e. the record operation conflict '51' (9.1.13.8 item 1). GR3's FOREVER alone lands '52', the deadlock 9.1.13.8 item 2 leaves the implementor to detect (A.1 item 109): the holder is a connector of the EXECUTING run unit and can never release while this statement runs, so GR3's 'until the input-output operation has been completed' would not terminate. EVIDENCE: conformance:cases/9.1.13.8-Record-operation-conflict-condition-with-unsuccessful/pb346_read_retry_record_conflict_2023 and its 2014 twin run all eight forms through BOTH read formats against a second connector's lock and are byte-identical (R2NONE/R2T0/R2TNEG/R2T2/R2S0/R2SNEG/R2S30 = 51, R2FVR = 52, and the same on the S1 sequential-access half), with the amounts held in DATA ITEMS so GR4 a)'s 'result of the evaluation' is a real runtime evaluation; the 0-SECONDS/30-SECONDS pair is the observable form of the A.1 item 166 determination on the RECORD class, as 2023/pb142_retry_conflict_class_ec is on the FILE SHARING class. unit:CobolFileLockTests.ReadUnderEveryRetryForm_BindsGR9ToTheRetryRules_OnBothFormats is the drift test for the READ's own binding to 14.7.9 (both formats x four forms); RetryLoop_LandsTheConflictsOwnStatus_ByClass is the class-rule drift test; ReadShared_SequentialOrdinals_Conflict51_AndAdvancingOnLockSkips covers half (i) with no phrase. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2014/2023 identical (Annex E lists no change to 14.9.30.4 GR9 or to 14.7.9), and both are evidenced by the twin goldens; the RETRY phrase is a COBOL-2002 introduction whose gating diagnostic below 2002 is COBOL0900, pinned by conformance:cases/_unassigned/retry_below_2002.
